ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and UBOs against UIAF national lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, INTERPOL notices, the Colombian Procuraduría disqualification registry, and the EU consolidated sanctions list. Adverse-media and PEP-sensitive-source screening is required at on-boarding and repeated on a monthly basis through an independent commercial screening service.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (www.rues.org.co) administered through the local Cámara de Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Spanish or contain a Spanish descriptor permitting clear identification. Foreign terms must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet, avoid confusion with existing Colombian names, and comply with commercial-name pronunciation rules established by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant must file a written reconsideration (recurso de reposición) with the issuing Cámara de Comercio within five business days, attaching a comparative registry report and evidence of non-confusing distinctiveness. If denied, a second-instance appeal may be submitted to the Superintendencia de Sociedades under the national administrative procedure law; a new name submission may also be filed immediately.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permitted for the administrative legal seat and mail collection, but cannot replace a physical operational establishment in Colombia for endoscope manufacturing. The INVIMA manufacturing license requires a physical production site with applicable sanitary, traceability and quality-control infrastructure. A virtual address is therefore acceptable only as an auxiliary registered-office address, not as the licensed manufacturing facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – approximately 75% probability of an unannounced physical or regulatory inspection during the first 12 months of operations, given medical-device sanitary licensing by INVIMA, periodic Cámara de Comercio verification, and DIAN tax-audit site visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Régimen Jurídico de la Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Article 5 and following; Commercial Code (Código de Comercio) provisions applicable to corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document) registered with the competent Chamber of Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for S.A.S.; founders may agree on capital and payment schedule. Capital must be paid up at least the percentage stipulated in the articles; if the contribution is in currency and exceeds the legal threshold, it must be deposited in a bank and evidenced by a certificate at formalization. An escrow account is not statutorily mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [SAS NAME] – FIRST MEETING. The organization, being duly constituted, adopts this organizational resolution: (1) The shares subscribed by the founding shareholders are hereby ratified and the capital paid in or pending in the terms set forth in the bylaws is expressly acknowledged. (2) The registered office of the company is established at [ADDRESS, CITY, COLOMBIA], and the Chamber of Commerce registration is instructed. (3) [NAME] is appointed as Legal Representative and [NAME] as Secretary, with the powers set out in the bylaws, and they are authorized to perform all acts necessary for the company's formalization, tax registration with DIAN, and commercial licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Name Availability Search and Pre-Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de la ciudad del domicilio social through the RUES online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online request to the RUES with at least three proposed corporate names. The Chamber verifies the name against existing trademarks and corporate records and issues a name availability certificate (Certificado de no homologación). No notarial protocol is required at this stage.
required_dossiers: Solicitud de nombre (name request form)
Cédula or passport of subscribing shareholders
Power of attorney, if submission is made through a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first name is rejected, submit the second or third alternate name; the request may be amended with alternative names without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization (if Required) of the S.A.S. Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría (notary) only when an escritura pública is required; otherwise executed privately by the shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and obtain signatures on the private document of incorporation containing the full bylaws, corporate purpose, share subscriptions, capital payment terms, registered office, term, board structure, internal fiduciary rules and designation of the legal representative. Notarization is not mandatory for S.A.S. unless the assets contributed include real property or a tax privilege requires a public instrument.
required_dossiers: Documento privado de constitución signed by all shareholders
Shareholders' identification documents
Tax IDs or passports of all founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry requires a notary due to real-property contributions or legal formality, convert the document into an escritura pública and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration in the Chamber of Commerce Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio local seccional — RUES office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed incorporation document with the Chamber of Commerce using Form RUES-0 for Mercantile Registration. Pay the registration fee based on the subscribed capital. The Chamber scans the document and issues a certificate of registration, providing a provisional NIT for the company.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation document
Form RUES-0 and annexes
Cédula or passport of the legal representative
Name availability certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration office raises an observation, correct the deficiency within 10 working days and file a corrective amendment; the file is then automatically reactivated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and RUT Issuance with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) — virtual tax window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, the legal representative must access the DIAN portal at www.dian.gov.co to obtain the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) and the definitive NIT. Confirm membership, download the RUT certificate, and activate mandatory e-invoicing parameters (factura electrónica).
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation issued by the Chamber of Commerce
Incorporation bylaws (copy)
Legal representative identification and provisional NIT (PRE-RUT)
Bank deposit certificate if capital contribution has been paid
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIAN portal requires biometric verification or shows inconsistency between Chamber and DIAN data, file a PQR (procedury) through the portal with reconciliation proof from the Chamber.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Deposit / Escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking institution authorized by the Financial Superintendence of Colombia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate current or savings account in the company's name. Deposits of cash capital contributions must be evidenced by a bank certificate when incorporation is being formalized. For an S.A.S. with zero capital, no deposit is required, but if a deposit is made, obtain a certificado de aporte for the corporate file.
required_dossiers: Company bylaws and certificate of existence
RUT / NIT
Legal representative's identification
Board minutes authorizing the bank account opening
Beneficial owners declaration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further beneficial ownership documentation, present the updated register of final beneficial owners (Registro de Beneficiario Final) and a written corporate chain declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation, Corporate Books, and Appointment Recording
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio and corporate administrative records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the final Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal from the Chamber of Commerce to confirm the legal representative's appointment. Then adopt and open the statutory corporate books: Libro de Actas, Libro de Registro de Accionistas, and share issuance documentation. Notarization of the books is optional but increases formality.
required_dossiers: Registration receipt from the Chamber of Commerce
Bylaws
Board minutes appointing the legal representative
Annotation of share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate of existence bears an incorrect representative data, file an amendment to the minutes at the Chamber and obtain a corrected certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: INVIMA (Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos) and the territorial Secretaría de Salud, together with the local municipal industrial licensing office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización Sanitaria de Funcionamiento como Fabricante de Dispositivos Médicos (Sanitary Authorization to Operate as a Medical Device Manufacturer) and Registro Sanitario per surgical laparoscopy tower model

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: ANLA (Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales) or the Regional Autonomous Corporation (CAR) when applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV — Registration and Declaration (Declaración de Vertimientos) rather than a full EIA, provided that the facility is located in an industrial zone with public sewer connection and wastewater discharge below the thresholds requiring a discharge permit. Otherwise a full environmental license is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 6-9, TSS below 200 mg/L, BOD5 below 400 mg/L for non-hazardous discharges into municipal sewers. Atmospheric/VOC emissions: comply with Resolución 2254 of 2017; use ventilation and capture systems in cleaning and disinfection areas and maintain VOC emission records. Hazardous waste must be managed under Decree 4741 of 2005.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Bomberos) from the municipal fire department; structural and load inspection certificate from the local planning authority; occupational risk assessment and workplace safety clearance through the ARL (Administradora de Riesgos Laborales) and the Ministry of Labour, including training on chemical handling and electrical safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – official web portal: https://www.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing a Colombian S.A.S. must obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) from DIAN before commencing local activities. For non-resident entities with no permanent establishment, a NIT can be obtained through a legal representative appointed for this purpose. Registration is performed electronically via DIAN’s Muisca system, requiring notarized incorporation documents (certificate of existence and legal representation), proof of address, and identification of the legal representative. After NIT issuance, the entity must register in the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) and may need to obtain a digital signature certificate for electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) and customs operations. The RUT must be updated whenever there is a change in address, activity codes, or responsible tax regime (e.g., VAT, ICA, withholding agent status).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a check-the-box or full pass-through election mechanism similar to the U.S. LLC regime. The S.A.S. is a separate taxable entity subject to corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta). However, the Colombian tax regime permits the following elections: (1) Income tax consolidation for business groups under Article 254 of the Tax Code, subject to DIAN authorization and 50% common ownership continuity; (2) Special economic sector tax regimes (e.g., free trade zones or Creative Economy VAT exemption elections); (3) Election between the special corporate income tax rate for solidarity societies/cooperatives (20%) and the general rate (35%), if applicable; (4) Optional quarterly or annual advance payment mechanisms for certain taxpayers. Hybrid mismatch rules follow BEPS Action 2 and can restrict deductibility of interest or royalty payments, but no formal election is provided to alter statutory classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold; obligatory VAT registration (RUT updated) for any person or entity selling taxable goods or services, including importers and exporters. The DIAN has simplified regimes for small taxpayers with gross assets or income thresholds, but exporters must register in the full responsible regime regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Colombia mandates full real-time electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta) through DIAN-authorized technology providers. Invoices must be transmitted to DIAN’s validation and clearance platform for authorization before delivery to the acquirer. Invoicing systems must integrate with DIAN’s APIs or use certified software. For exports, the electronic export representation is supported by the SICE (Sistema Informático de Comercio Exterior) for customs declarations. Specific requirements include electronic invoice XML schemas, CUFE/CUDE digital stamping, and humidity/signature verification. Taxpayers must also issue electronic supporting documents (documento soporte en adquisiciones a no responsables). Failure to comply with electronic invoicing mandates results in fines and possible prohibition of export operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Colombian VAT law (Estatuto Tributario, Articles 481 and 481-472) allows zero-rating (0% VAT) for exports of goods, including medical devices such as endoscopic towers and rigid endoscopes. Eligibility requires that the goods be physically exported and sold to a foreign purchaser, leaving Colombian customs territory. Services sold to foreign recipients that are used exclusively abroad may also be zero-rated if they meet territorial and technical export criteria. The taxpayer must hold an active RUT status as an exporter, and the sale must be evidenced by valid customs export documentation proving the goods passed through customs control. No VAT is charged on the invoice; export VAT credits from purchases may be refunded or offset by DIAN.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Formulario de Declaración de Exportación (DEX) / Export Declaration via SICE
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (shipping document)
Commercial Invoice Proforma / Final Invoice indicating export and HS code 9018.90 (endoscopic surgical instruments)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa) or bank transfer proof of foreign currency payment
Lista de empaque (Packing List) and certificate of origin if applicable
Registered RUT schedule for export operations
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN has extensive audit powers over zero-rated exports. If export operations are not fully substantiated, or if the goods are diverted back to the local market, DIAN can retrospectively reverse the zero-rating, assess unpaid VAT plus default interest, and impose penalties up to 200% of the omitted tax under Article 648 of the Tax Code. Fraudulent claims may trigger criminal tax evasion proceedings (penalties of imprisonment for up to 9 years under Law 1778/2016 and Article 434 of the Criminal Code). Additionally, exporters must repatriate foreign currency within 6 months (180 days) to maintain export incentives; failure to repatriate can lead to loss of the zero-rating status, forced inclusion of gross revenue as taxable income, and fines under foreign exchange regulation (Estatuto Cambiario).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia) as monetary, exchange-control and international investment registration authority, with coordinated enforcement by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) for supervised banking intermediaries and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) for customs and exchange-infringement sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a free-floating, unified foreign-exchange regime (Régimen Cambiario) under which all resident cross-border currency transactions must be channeled through authorized intermediaries of the exchange market (IMCs). Current-account items, including import payments, freight, royalties, technical assistance and profit/dividend remittances, are fully convertible subject to presentation of the underlying commercial documentation and electronic exchange declaration. Capital-account items, including foreign direct investment (FDI) equity injections and external credits, are equally permissible but require mandatory registration with Banco de la República through the IMC (Certificado de Registro de Inversiones Internacionales). Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted provided the FDI registration remains current, the corporate dividend minutes are executed, and the payment flows through an IMC under the applicable dividend concept code; statutory non-resident dividend withholding must be applied by the Colombian payer. The COP has no dual-rate system, no prior-import-license exchange gate, and no administrative convertibility permit for the targeted surgical-laparoscopy-tower business; legal convertibility risk is concentrated in documentary compliance rather than in availability of foreign currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds for goods must be channeled, at 100% of the invoiced value, through an authorized IMC within a maximum statutory collection term of 18 months from the date of the customs export declaration (DEX), extendable to 24 months only upon express prior authorization from Banco de la República. Upon receipt, the foreign currency must enter Colombia via the IMC, where it may be credited to a registered foreign-currency account or converted to COP at the IMC spot rate; conversion to COP is not in all cases legally mandatory, but the proceeds must remain within the IMC reporting perimeter or within a pre-registered foreign-currency cuenta de compensación abroad until the export obligation is closed in the Declaración de Cambio Form 3. If the repatriation term is missed, the exporter must purchase the equivalent foreign currency in the local market to regularize the operation and settle the foreign-exchange infringement penalty administrated by DIAN and Banco de la República. The sales contract for each laparoscopy tower shipment must evidence the 0-18 month payment term, and the INVIMA export certificate and DEX customs filing must accompany the banking file to avoid misclassification of proceeds as portfolio or non-trade income.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (COP and USD) with IMC FX desk, FDI registration service, and trade-finance products; Capital Escrow Account not applicable under Colombian law.
Operational Account (COP and USD) with documentary letter-of-credit issuance, FX forwards, and external debt registration; Capital Escrow Account not applicable.
Operational Account (COP) with corporate sweep accounts, commercial LC desk, and IMC exchange-declaration support; Capital Escrow Account not applicable.
Operational Account (COP) with derivative forwards desk, international trade services and IMC registration capabilities; Capital Escrow Account not applicable.
Operational Account (COP/USD) positioned for Canada and US-Colombia-LatAm corridor clearing, with trade finance and IMC services; Capital Escrow Account not applicable.
Operational Account (COP) with regional corporate banking, FX wiring and import payment processing; Capital Escrow Account not applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail and strictly ancillary as a wallet/payment rail. Neither domestic fintech e-money institutions (e.g., Nequi, Bancolombia digital wallet) nor offshore EMIs (Wise, Mercury, Dukascopy, Airwallex) qualify as authorized intermediaries of the Colombian exchange market (IMC). Consequently, they cannot legally receive or settle inbound FDI equity, export proceeds, or documentary trade collections for the Colombian SAS. Channeling such flows through a non-IMC digital bank would constitute a foreign-exchange violation (infracción cambiaria) enforceable by DIAN and Banco de la República, with fines calculated on the transaction amount. Offshore EMIs are viable only for minor operational disbursements (SaaS subscriptions, digital advertising, travel, and small logistics costs) that do not require an exchange declaration and are fully recorded in the Colombian accounting books; this corridor should never carry invoiced trade payments or capital movements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default and practically mandatory requirement. For an SAS with non-resident UBOs and no prior local banking record, Tier-1 Colombian banks apply SFC CDD/AML rules requiring at least one legal representative or director to appear in person at the branches (Bancolombia at Medellín or Bogotá; Banco de Bogotá at Bogotá) for the corporate onboarding interview, signature verification and transaction-profile setting. Fully remote opening is not offered for cross-border manufacturing companies. A notarized and apostilled 'poder especial' can vest treasury-signing authority in a resident manager and reduce the initial visit to a single signatory, but the UBO will typically still be asked to participate in a video interview and to submit certified corporate records and source-of-funds evidence. Implementation roadmap: incorporate the SAS, obtain Chamber of Commerce certification and RUT, open the account with one physical visit, and complete IMC registration before the first inbound capital wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete identification of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) or multi-jurisdictional holding layers without transparent ownership chains.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate structure chart, sworn UBO declaration under Colombian corporate rules, apostilled and translated share registers, audited group financial statements, fiscal residence certificates, and personal source-of-wealth letters with supporting bank references for each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP (politically exposed person) status of any shareholder, director, or family member controlling the SAS.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP screening questionnaire, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth breakdown, FATCA/CRS self-certifications, publicly documented career history, and evidence that wealth accumulation is unrelated to any public office or procurement function.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of the Mercantile Registry (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each year for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incremental fines of approximately COP 1.0–1.5 SMLMV (≈USD 240–360) per month of delay; failure to renew for two consecutive years triggers strike-off from the registry (cancelación de la matrícula) and loss of formal merchant status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between August 11 and August 24 of the year following the fiscal year-end, according to the last digit of the entity's NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly default interest of approximately 2.2% from the original due date; late-filing penalty of 5% of the tax assessed; omissions or inaccuracies subject to fines of 20%–160% of the omitted tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Certified Annual Financial Statements with the Chamber of Commerce (Estados Financieros Certificados)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades via the local Chamber of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By September 30 of the year following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of up to approximately USD 1,200 per unfiled obligation; persistent non-compliance restricts corporate legal capacity, banking facilities, and subsequent registry renewals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' General Meeting for Approval of Annual Accounts and Corporate Acts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance record registered in the Shareholders' Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months following each fiscal year-end (no later than March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve annual accounts blocks lawful dividend distributions; directors and shareholders become exposed to private enforcement actions and regulatory sanction by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation and Update of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales — RUB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days following the anniversary of the initial RUB filing; immediate update required upon any shareholding or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to approximately COP 142 million (≈USD 34,000) for false, incomplete, or late UBO disclosure; DIAN may suspend tax-clearance certificates and impose restrictions on the entity's tax records.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) is required for S.A.S. companies whose total assets exceed COP 5,000 SMLMV (≈USD 1.7 million) or whose gross annual operating income exceeds COP 3,000 SMLMV (≈USD 1.0 million); S.A.S. legal entities designated by law, or those whose accounting records fall under per-association commercial rules, are likewise subject to mandatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian Financial Reporting Standards (Marco Técnico Normativo, DUR 2420 of 2015), fully aligned with IFRS: full IFRS for Group 1 large entities and IFRS-for-SMEs for most S.A.S. manufacturers; annual financial statements must be prepared on a going-concern basis, certified by the legal representative and a licensed public accountant, and filed in accordance with commercial registry requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must maintain an up-to-date Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) at DIAN and confirm it annually within 30 calendar days after the anniversary date of the last ordinary filing. Any direct or indirect transfer of at least 10% of capital, voting rights, profits, or ultimate control—including issuance of new shares under the S.A.S. regime—must be reported to DIAN within 30 calendar days of the transaction. The legal representative bears certification liability for accuracy and timeliness.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 1,000 per year (registered domicile address and compliance agent for annual renewals)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 8,000 per year (certified independent audit when the statutory thresholds are met)

stage_6.entry_description: Total gross revenue from Colombian-source operations, including sales of endoscope towers and components, service and maintenance fees, and exports; accrued under P.C.G.A. Colombia (full IFRS basis).
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record all revenue attributable to the Colombian S.A.S. even if invoiced from/paid by related overseas distributors; exclude revenue of foreign related parties (no permanent establishment presumption without factual local nexus).
